recognizance

rih-KOG-nih-zunss · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Recognizance is a formal promise made to a court, often to appear at a future date.

Out of an abundance of caution, the magistrate still required a small bond even after accepting the young man's recognizance.

Worked Example

The visiting student, arrested for a minor traffic violation, was freed on recognizance after promising in writing to appear at his court date before flying home.

A recognizance is essentially a formal, on-the-record promise to the court -- no money changes hands, but breaking it has serious consequences.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

pledge: A pledge is a solemn promise you can make anywhere -- you pledge allegiance, pledge a donation, pledge to do better. A recognizance is one specific, technical kind of pledge: a promise formally recorded by a court, usually to appear on a set date, with legal penalties for breaking it.

vow: A vow is a deeply personal, serious promise -- wedding vows, a vow of silence -- binding on your honor and conscience rather than in law. A recognizance binds in law: it is a promise entered in a court's record, and breaking it carries real legal consequences.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

forfeiture: the loss of something as a penalty for failing to comply

noncompliance: failure to act as required or promised

Where it sits · how much legal weight the commitment carries — promise → recognizance → bond

promise vs. recognizance: A promise is a casual, spoken commitment with no legal weight behind it, while a recognizance turns a promise into something a court records and can enforce.

bond vs. recognizance: A bond is an actual, money-backed guarantee -- a stronger, more formal commitment than a plain recognizance.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-

prefix — re-: again, intensively (Latin)

root — cogniz-

root — cogniz-: to know (from Latin cognoscere, 'to get to know')

suffix — -ance

suffix — -ance: the act or state of; forms a noun (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Recognizance is built from re- ('again') + cogniz- ('to know,' from Latin cognoscere) + -ance (a noun ending: 'the act or state of') -- it's built the same way as the word recognize, and originally meant a formally acknowledged, on-the-record promise.

Use the root in a new word: incognito

Use the root in a new word: incognito: The movie star traveled incognito, wearing a plain hat and sunglasses so no one would recognize her.

Word Choice

Recognizance is a legal term -- you'll almost always see it in the fixed phrase 'released on one's own recognizance,' rarely anywhere else.
